chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washshā’, from Abān, from ‘Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ‘Abdillāh, who said:
I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about a man who forgot a salat (prayer) until the time of another salat (prayer) entered, so he said:

“If he forgets the salat (prayer) or sleeps through it, he performs it when he remembers it. If he remembers it while he is in a salat (prayer), he begins with the one he forgot. If he remembers it while he is with an Imam in salat al-maghrib, he completes it with one rak‘ah, then performs al-maghrib, then performs al-‘atamah afterward. If he had performed al-‘atamah alone and had prayed two rak‘ahs of it, then remembered that he had forgotten al-maghrib, he completes it with one rak‘ah, so that the salat (prayer) of al-maghrib becomes three rak‘ahs, then he performs al-‘atamah after that.”

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader with whom one is praying in congregation
key_terms.الْعَتَمَةَ: the night salat (prayer), referring here to al-‘ishā’
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the sunset salat (prayer), consisting of three rak‘ahs
key_terms.صَلَاةً: a prescribed salat (prayer) that was missed
key_terms.نَسِيَ: forgot; failed to remember the obligation at its proper time
key_terms.يَذْكُرُهَا: remembers it; becomes aware of the missed prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they remember a missed prayer after beginning another prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for a missed salat (prayer) that is remembered after the time of another prayer has entered. It establishes that the forgotten prayer should be performed upon remembering it and details how to proceed if one remembers during another prayer, especially in the case of al-maghrib and al-‘atamah.
